The Beckmann rearrangement is an important organic chemistry reaction that involves the acid-catalyzed rearrangement of ketoximes. In this reaction:

1. A ketoxime (R₂C=NOH) undergoes rearrangement under acidic conditions
2. The reaction involves migration of one of the groups attached to the carbon of the C=N bond
3. This migration occurs with simultaneous loss of water

The key product that forms in an acid-catalyzed Beckmann rearrangement of ketoximes is an amide (R-CO-NH-R'). This is a well-established organic chemistry transformation where the nitrogen of the oxime becomes the nitrogen of the amide in the product.

The general reaction can be represented as:
R₂C=NOH + H⁺ → R-CO-NH-R'
